rows.title: The tide is turning in the housing market as top metro areas see home prices fall ahead of a broader decline later this year
rows.standfirst: Home-sale prices in 11 of the 50 biggest U.S. metro areas are already falling, according to data from Redfin.

rows.title: Meta wants to replace its human workers with AI to review privacy and societal risks
rows.standfirst: Up to 90% of risk assessments could become automated. Other companies like Klarna, Salesforce, and Duolingo are looking at job shifts in the face of AI.

rows.title: Swiss inflation turns negative for first time in four years
rows.standfirst: Inflation was pushed down by heating oil and air transport, while rents and some fruit and vegetable costs rose, the Swiss National Bank said.

rows.title: America’s prized ‘exceptionalism’ is the collateral damage of Trump’s tariff war, says Deutsche Bank
rows.standfirst: “The structural foundations of U.S. exceptionalism—particularly the ability to finance itself cheaply via the dollar’s reserve status—have begun to erode,” wrote Deutsche Bank.

rows.title: Fewer people are quitting their jobs right now—but layoffs are on the rise
rows.standfirst: Uncertainty in the economy means more people are trying to stay in their jobs, so long as employers choose to keep them around.

rows.title: Trump hiring freeze threatens key economic data as the Fed zeroes in on inflation
rows.standfirst: The staff cutbacks have intensified worries among economists that government spending cuts could degrade the federal government’s ability to compile crucial economic data.

rows.title: Anthropic researchers predict a ‘pretty terrible decade’ for humans as AI could wipe out white collar jobs
rows.standfirst: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has said that AI may soon take over half of all entry-level office jobs.

rows.title: European Central Bank cuts rate to 2% amid struggling eurozone growth and stable inflation
rows.standfirst: The European Central Bank said inflation of 1.9% was now around target, dropping the previous language that it was merely “on track”.

rows.title: Young people are frozen out of the housing market—this outdated tax law is a big reason why
rows.standfirst: It’s unintentionally keeping young people out of the market as older owners refuse to sell, says one real estate agent.

rows.title: Trade wars have Americans so nervous even six-figure earners are flocking to dollar stores
rows.standfirst: Strained consumers are turning toward discount retailers amid tariffs and inflation.

rows.title: Hiring is slowing but still solid, with 139,000 jobs added last month
rows.standfirst: The full effects of massive tariffs likely have not been felt yet, but the job market has clearly slowed.

rows.title: Top Google exec says AI will rival humans in just 5 years and predicts we’ll ‘colonize the galaxy’ in 2030—but he draws the line at robot nurses
rows.standfirst: 2030 will be “an era of maximum human flourishing, where we travel to the stars and colonize the galaxy,” Google DeepMind CEO says. Bill Gates and Marc Benioff have shared similar predictions.

rows.title: A hot trend in the housing market is Gen Z buying homes with siblings
rows.standfirst: BofA found that 22% of Gen Z homeowners bought their home with siblings, surging from 12% in 2024 and just 4% in 2023.

rows.title: Klarna CEO predicts AI-driven job displacement will cause a recession
rows.standfirst: Sebastian Siemiatkowski foresees mass AI-induced headcount reductions among white-collar workers.

rows.title: Fannie and Freddie could make hedge funds a huge payday if they go public. One expert wants a ‘utility model’ for the Fortune 500 giants
rows.standfirst: Billionaire Trump backers Bill Ackman and John Paulson are among the investors who could win big.

rows.title: Starbucks is hiring a fully remote dream role: making six figures to travel the world, make TikToks, and drink coffee
rows.standfirst: The job has a six-figure salary and bonus, doesn’t require a college degree, and is completely remote—a perfect fit for chronically online Gen Z.

rows.title: Goldman Sachs wants students to stop using ChatGPT in job interviews with the bank
rows.standfirst: Anthropic and Amazon have also warned job-seekers about using AI tools, even disqualifying applicants if they’re caught.

rows.title: World Bank warns the global economy is barreling toward its weakest decade in 50 years
rows.standfirst: The World Bank cut growth forecasts for 70% of global economies.

rows.title: New grads are struggling to find jobs and they’re being locked out of the labor market because of 3 key factors
rows.standfirst: “Entry-level roles are in short supply.”

rows.title: Recurring jobless claims spike to highest level since 2021 at 1.96 million
rows.standfirst: The numbers indicate unemployed people are taking longer to get back into the job market.

rows.title: Jamie Dimon says inflation will go up and employment will shift down as economy ‘deteriorates’ amid shifting ‘tectonic plates’
rows.standfirst: Jamie Dimon says there’s no point looking at consumer sentiment for a hint on the economy. Analysts will have to wait for the real data to trickle through.

rows.title: NYC landlords can’t require tenants to pay broker fees anymore
rows.standfirst: Though there was technically no cap on these fees, they averaged around 12% to 15% of the annual rent of the listing.

rows.title: Trump says he won’t fire Powell, but again demands rate cut
rows.standfirst: Fed officials are expected to hold interest rates steady at their two-day policy meeting next week.

rows.title: Oil prices surge after Israel’s attack on Iran. Trump urges Iran to ‘make a deal before there is nothing left’
rows.standfirst: JPMorgan fears crude oil could hit a high of $130 a barrel, causing U.S. inflation to return to 5% in a worst-case scenario.

rows.title: ‘College doesn’t carry the same ROI it once did’: 70% of teens say their parents support them going to trade school or getting an apprenticeship
rows.standfirst: Parents are becoming more accepting of alternative post-high-school plans.

rows.title: LinkedIn cofounder Reid Hoffman admits what you learn during college may not matter—it’s this skill that can help Gen Z land entry-level jobs
rows.standfirst: The billionaire entrepreneur says Gen Z job-seekers would be better off leveraging AI tools and their connections if they want to land a job right now.

rows.title: Israel’s attacks on Iran may keep Fed rate cuts on hold, just as inflation was looking better
rows.standfirst: The 10-year Treasury yield jumped 6.9 basis points on Friday to $4.426, reversing a dip in the immediate aftermath of the attacks.

rows.title: Canva’s cofounder is looking to hire ‘AI natives’ and university dropouts to train the rest of the company on the tech
rows.standfirst: “They’re really good hires, especially when you add them to a nontechnical team and upskill the rest of the organization,” Cliff Obrecht said. “[They] become evangelists in the organization and really help drive that mindset shift.”

rows.title: New graduates are having such a hard time finding jobs they’re now having an ‘oversize’ impact on America’s unemployment rate
rows.standfirst: Landing a job is only getting more difficult for graduates, potentially strengthening arguments from the likes of Jamie Dimon about focusing on job-ready skills as opposed to college degrees.

rows.title: Central banks expect to swap out more of their U.S. dollar reserves for gold as greenback’s safe-haven status weakens
rows.standfirst: Those in the Global South are actively shifting their own reserves toward gold at a much faster rate than advanced economies to reduce their U.S. dollar exposure amid growing trade protectionism.

rows.title: Retail CEO says orders from big-box stores are down 40% because they have no idea how shoppers are going to react to price hikes
rows.standfirst: “Shoppers are very price sensitive,” said Paul Cosaro, who founded his California company 40 years ago.

rows.title: The ‘Godfather of AI’ says this sector will be safe from being replaced by tech—but even then, only the ‘very skilled’ will hold down a job
rows.standfirst: Ex-Google AI boss Geoffery Hinton has a stark prediction for workers: Most of you are about to get replaced. Anthropic’s and Klarna’s CEOs have issued similar warnings.

rows.title: Amazon’s Jassy says AI will reduce company’s corporate ranks
rows.standfirst: Andy Jassy expects the company’s workforce to decline in the next few years.

rows.title: Fed meets as policymakers are expected to assert their independence amid Trump’s pressure
rows.standfirst: After a turbulent spring, investors will be watching this latest Fed meeting to see if Chair Jerome Powell will offer any hints about whether the worst has passed or is yet to come.

rows.title: War, tariffs, and Trump: What members of the FOMC will be thinking as they finalize their base rate decision today
rows.standfirst: ANALYSIS: Here are a handful of factors likely impacting the Fed’s interest rate decision being announced today.

rows.title: Reid Hoffman says consoling Gen Z in the AI bloodbath is like putting a ‘Band-Aid on a bullet wound’—he shares 4 skills college grads need to survive
rows.standfirst: The billionaire tech founder tells Gen Z the secret to surviving the AI job bloodbath isn’t mastering prompts—but rather leaning on the human skills tech can’t replicate.

rows.title: The Fed holds interest rates steady and forecasts two rate cuts for 2025
rows.standfirst: Faced with a blurry forecast for the U.S. economy, the Federal Reserve continued its pattern of keeping interest rates at their current levels.

rows.title: Stocks are flat, as the Fed’s latest forecast flirts with stagflation
rows.standfirst: The Federal Reserve’s quarterly projection included lower growth and higher inflation; the Fed also maintained its previous expectation of two interest rate cuts.

rows.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says AI can rival someone with a PhD—just weeks after saying it’s ready for entry-level jobs. So what’s left for grads?
rows.standfirst: As Amazon, OpenAI and Anthropic bosses warn, entry-level corporate jobs are about to get cut, experts say Gen Z don’t need to panic—yet.

rows.title: Fed governor breaks ranks and says rate cuts could resume next month to prevent further cracks in the job market
rows.standfirst: “If you’re starting to worry about the downside risk to the labor market, move now, don’t wait,” Waller told CNBC.

rows.title: Fed’s Daly says next rate cut more likely in the fall
rows.standfirst: “By then, we’ll have quite a bit more information, and businesses are telling me that’s what they’re going to look to for some resolution.”

rows.title: This millennial was rejected from 200 jobs—now he makes millions charging wealthy families six-figures to get their kids into the Ivy Leagues
rows.standfirst: Meet the millennial admissions consultant charging up to $750,000 to help students get into Harvard, Stanford, and MIT.

rows.title: Russia’s economy boomed after the invasion of Ukraine—it’s now running out of steam
rows.standfirst: Record-low unemployment and ultra-hot inflation have put Russia “on the brink” of a recession, its economy minister said.

rows.title: LinkedIn COO says the bottom rung of Gen Z’s job ladder isn’t breaking because of AI—but it is evolving
rows.standfirst: LinkedIn COO Dan Shapero told Fortune in Cannes: “Navigating the transition to an AI economy is probably going to be the issue of the next decade.”

rows.title: Ireland sees thousands of jobs at risk from U.S. pharma tariffs
rows.standfirst: Ireland is running a strong fiscal surplus, driven by corporate taxes from U.S. multinationals like Apple and Pfizer. However, global slowdown and tariff uncertainty put much of that revenue at risk.

rows.title: Gen Z is facing a job-market bloodbath—but JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon says employers are still chasing students who studied these fields
rows.standfirst: The billionaire JPMorgan Chase CEO isn’t wrong about the value of studying computer science—research shows that it can increase earnings by 8%.

rows.title: Ceasefire between Israel and Iran already being tested as markets bet it will stave off ‘stagflationary shock’
rows.standfirst: The rapidly unfolding events whipsawed world markets that briefly appeared to have avoided an oil shock and the uncertainty of a wider Middle East conflict.

rows.title: Federal Reserve governor Michelle Bowman says bank should consider cutting rate in July because tariff effects may be smaller than expected
rows.standfirst: Bowman said that President Donald Trump’s tariffs have so far not caused the jump in inflation that many economists feared, and any upcoming increase in prices would likely be just a one-time rise.

rows.title: A quarter of Americans now say they need to make at least $150,000 to feel secure—and inflation is largely to blame
rows.standfirst: Inflation has fueled a need for higher wages, but perceptions have also played a part, say experts.

rows.title: Trump urges Congress to grill ‘very dumb, hardheaded’ Powell in latest attack over Fed’s refusal to cut interest rates
rows.standfirst: Trump claimed that Americans will be paying for Powell’s “incompetence” for years to come, while the FOMC has maintained it needs greater clarity before lowering the base rate.

rows.title: Amazon to create thousands of new U.K. jobs as part of $54 billion investment—PM Starmer calls the deal ‘another major win’
rows.standfirst: “It means thousands of new jobs—real opportunities for people in every corner of the country to build careers, learn new skills, and support their families,” said Starmer.

rows.title: The Fed won’t lower rates like Trump wants because it sees ‘meaningful’ inflation spike later this year
rows.standfirst: Fed Chair Jerome Powell told Congress he expects an inflation surge—but how long and how high is unknown.

rows.title: New JPMorgan survey finds rising recession fears at mid-sized firms
rows.standfirst: One quarter of C-suite execs predict a recession, though most are bullish about their own business

rows.title: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan is prioritizing ‘profits and purpose’
rows.standfirst: “You can have great returns for your shareholders and do well for the communities you serve,” Moynihan told Fortune.

rows.title: Rate debate among the Fed has analysts questioning who’s ‘auditioning’ for Powell’s job already
rows.standfirst: President Trump has said he may move up the announcement of Powell’s replacement, with analysts looking for public debate among FOMC members for clues as to who is “auditioning” for the role.

rows.title: Federal judge orders Labor Department to keep Job Corps residential program for low-income youth running for now
rows.standfirst: Founded in 1964, Job Corps aims to help teenagers and young adults who struggled to finish traditional high school and find jobs.

rows.title: The Trump administration just took a big step toward considering crypto assets during home loan applications
rows.standfirst: The directive is “in keeping with President Trump’s vision to make the United States the crypto capital of the world.”

rows.title: New York is America’s worst place for a ‘cheap date.’ Here are the best cities to be romantic on a budget
rows.standfirst: Renters in the Big Apple also have much less money to splurge, according to an annual report from the Deutsche Bank Research Institute.

rows.title: Business leaders are threatening to leave New York City amid the unlikely ascension of Zohran Mamdani. This scenario has played out before—here’s what happened
rows.standfirst: By backing a platform of economic redistribution, New Yorkers are committing “suicide by Mayor,” one finance analyst said.

rows.title: Fortune 500 giants Nike and Walmart are warning of upcoming price hikes, but tariff-wary Americans are already pulling back on spending
rows.standfirst: A key inflation gauge moved higher in May in the latest sign that prices remain stubbornly elevated.

rows.title: Consumers saw a double whammy of bad news in May, pulling back on spending as inflation heated up
rows.standfirst: The economic bad vibes are hitting home.

rows.title: Falling home prices are raising the risk of a deeper correction as the housing market cracks under high mortgage rates
rows.standfirst: The latest Case-Shiller home price report showed a 0.3% monthly fall in the 20-city index in April, steeper than March’s downwardly revised 0.2% dip.

rows.title: This Gen X CEO has only worked at one company for 35 years—she says job-hopping Gen Z are not putting enough energy and time into their current gigs
rows.standfirst: Staying curious—and not worrying about what’s coming in 10 years—has been part of ACT CEO Janet Godwin’s secret for success.

rows.title: ‘Twilight’ superfans bought Bella Swan’s house for $360,000—now they get $140,000 a year in gross revenue renting out the ultimate collector’s item
rows.standfirst: “Twilight” captured the hearts of millennials in 2008. Now, 17 years since its release, its fans are all grown up with “big-boy money”—and one couple is crashing Airbnb with the listing.

rows.title: Zohran Mamdani doesn’t think there should be billionaires but would work with them as NYC mayor and denies being a communist
rows.standfirst: “I don’t think that we should have billionaires, because, frankly, it is so much money in a moment of such inequality,” Mamdani said.
